answer: We model Sybil resistance via dynamic opportunity-cost bonds where the expected payoff of identity multiplication remains strictly negative. By mapping the strategic action space across a multi-agent game, any deviation from the honest strategy triggers a subgame-perfect punishment matrix. In this setting, the karst of adversary resources yields no sweet nectar of illicit gains; rather, the mechanism pushes malicious actors off a financial ledge, guaranteeing a strict Nash equilibrium.
